learn.title: What is π (pi)?
learn.html:
Measure any circle. Divide the circumference by the diameter. You always get about 3.14.

This number is called π (we say "pie"). We use π ≈ 3.14 or π ≈ 22/7.

The question always tells you which one to use.

learn.title: Circumference formula
learn.html:
Circumference = π × diameter

The diameter is 2 radii, so also: Circumference = 2 × π × radius

So the circumference is a bit more than 3 times the diameter.

learn.title: Semicircles and quarter circles
learn.html:
An arc is part of the circumference.

Semicircle: arc = ½ of the circumference. Perimeter = arc + diameter.

Quarter circle: arc = ¼ of the circumference. Perimeter = arc + radius + radius.

learn.title: Semicircle, diameter 10 cm (π ≈ 3.14)
learn.html:
Arc = ½ × 3.14 × 10 = 15.7 cm

Perimeter = 15.7 + 10 = 25.7 cm (don't forget the straight edge!)

learn.title: Area of a circle
learn.html:
Cut a circle into many thin slices and line them up. They make a shape like a rectangle.

Its length is half the circumference (π × r) and its width is the radius (r).

Area of a circle = π × r × r (we write πr²)

learn.title: A circle on a 10 cm square
learn.html:
The circle fits the square, so the diameter is 10 cm and the radius is 5 cm.

Area ≈ 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 cm²

learn.title: Watch out: radius, not diameter!
learn.html:
The formula uses the radius. If you are given the diameter, halve it first.

Diameter 42 cm → radius 21 cm.

learn.title: Shaded ring
learn.html:
Big circle: 3.14 × 15 × 15 = 706.5 cm²
Small circle: 3.14 × 8 × 8 = 200.96 cm²

Shaded part = 706.5 - 200.96 = 505.54 cm²

learn.title: Semicircle and quarter circle
learn.html:
Semicircle, diameter 42 cm (π ≈ 22/7): ½ × 22/7 × 21 × 21 = 693 cm²

Quarter circle, radius 4 cm (π ≈ 3.14): ¼ × 3.14 × 4 × 4 = 12.56 cm²

questions.why: Area uses the radius, multiplied by itself, then by π.

learn.title: Circumference or area?
learn.html:
Going around the edge (a fence, a trim, a wheel turning) → circumference.

Covering the inside (paint, paper, grass) → area.

learn.title: Emma's paper circle
learn.html: Diameter 14 cm, so radius 7 cm. Area ≈ 3.14 × 7 × 7 = 153.86 cm²

learn.title: A circular field
learn.html: Diameter 12.5 m. Circumference ≈ 3.14 × 12.5 = 39.25 m

learn.title: Wheels
learn.html:
In 1 complete turn, a wheel rolls a distance equal to its circumference.

Distance = circumference × number of turns

learn.title: Running tracks
learn.html:
The 2 curved ends of a track make 1 whole ring. The straight parts are rectangles.

Track area = (big circle - small circle) + the rectangles.

learn.title: Track 2 m wide
learn.html:
Big circle radius 26 m, small circle radius 24 m.

Curved parts ≈ 3.14 × 26 × 26 - 3.14 × 24 × 24 = 2,122.64 - 1,808.64 = 314 m²

Straight parts = 2 × 100 × 2 = 400 m². Track ≈ 314 + 400 = 714 m²

questions.label: Do and Learn 1
questions.q: The figure shows a triangle inside a semicircle. The base of the triangle is 20 cm. Find the shaded area of the figure. (Correct to 2 decimal places.) (Take π ≈ 22/7.)
questions.hint: Shaded = semicircle - triangle. The triangle's height is a radius.
steps: The base (20 cm) is the diameter, so the radius = 10 cm.
Triangle: base 20 cm, height 10 cm (a radius). ½ × 20 × 10 = 100 cm²
questions.why: Semicircle minus the triangle inside it.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (a)
questions.q:
The figure shows 2 identical circles touching each other. The radius of each circle is 10 cm. (Take π ≈ 3.14.)
(a) Find the perimeter of the shaded part.
questions.hint: The shaded part has 2 straight edges and 2 curved edges. The 2 curves make 1 whole circle.
steps: The 2 curved edges are 2 half circles = 1 whole circumference.
The 2 straight edges are each a diameter: 20 + 20 = 40 cm
questions.why: 1 circumference plus 2 diameters.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (b)
questions.q:
The figure shows 2 identical circles touching each other. The radius of each circle is 10 cm. (Take π ≈ 3.14.)
(b) Find the area of the shaded part.
questions.hint: Shaded = the square between the centers - the 2 half circles (1 whole circle).
steps: The square between the 2 centers is 20 cm by 20 cm: 20 × 20 = 400 cm²
The 2 white half circles make 1 circle: 3.14 × 10 × 10 = 314 cm²
questions.why: Square minus one whole circle.

learn.title: Unit 11 big ideas
learn.html:
Circumference = π × d = 2 × π × r.

Area = π × r × r.

Use the π the question gives: 22/7 or 3.14.

learn.title: Pizza puzzle (p.176)
learn.html:
A large pizza (diameter 16 cm) has radius 8 cm: area ≈ 3.14 × 64 = 200.96 cm².

A small pizza (diameter 8 cm) has radius 4 cm: area ≈ 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm².

Double the diameter gives 4 times the area!

questions.label: Let's Think Along
questions.q: The figure below shows a path that is 4 m wide throughout. The path is made up of identical small semicircles where the distances A, B and C are 26 m each. Siti and Janice started walking from the opposite ends of the path. Siti walked along the red edge of the path and Janice walked along the green edge of the path. Find the difference in the distance that Siti and Janice walked. Give the answer in terms of π.
questions.hint: Each edge has big semicircles (diameter 26 + 4 + 4) and small ones (diameter 26).
steps: Big semicircle diameter = 26 + 4 + 4 = 34 m. Small semicircle diameter = 26 m.
Siti (red) walks 2 big semicircles + 1 small one + the 2 straight ends (17 m + 17 m):
Janice (green) walks 2 small semicircles + 1 big one + 34 m: π × 26 + ½ × π × 34 + 34 = 26π + 17π + 34 = 43π + 34 m
questions.why: The 34 m of straight ends cancel out, leaving 47π - 43π = 4π.

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: 2 identical wheels that are 7.18 m apart have radius 7 cm each as shown. They move toward each other. Each wheel takes 2 seconds to make 1 full turn. How long will it take for the 2 wheels to meet if they rotate at the same rate? (Take π ≈ 22/7.)
questions.hint: Change 7.18 m to cm first. The wheels meet when their edges touch, not their centers.
steps: 7.18 m = 718 cm. The 2 radii (7 cm + 7 cm = 14 cm) are not covered: 718 - 14 = 704 cm to cover.
1 turn of 1 wheel ≈ 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm. Both wheels in 2 seconds: 44 × 2 = 88 cm
questions.why: Together the wheels close 88 cm every 2 seconds, and 704 ÷ 88 = 8.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q: How is the area of a circle related to the area of a rectangle? Janice and Peter do an activity to find out. Both of them use an identical circle with radius r cm. Janice cuts her circle into parts and arranges them as shown. Peter cuts his circle into parts and arranges them as shown. Whose arrangement will show an area that is closer to the area of the rectangle? Explain.
questions.hint: Who cut the circle into more, smaller pieces?
steps: Peter cut his circle into many small slices. Janice cut hers into a few big slices.
Small slices line up almost straight, so Peter's shape looks almost exactly like a rectangle.
Janice's big slices leave wider gaps, so her shape is not as close to a rectangle.
questions.why: The smaller the slices, the closer the shape is to a rectangle of length πr and width r.
